reason: The text explicitly contradicts this statement. God's primary concern throughout this passage is for the Hebrew people, not just the leaders. Key evidence: (1) God 'heard their groaning' (וַיִּשְׁמַע אֱלֹהִים אֶת־ נַאֲקָתָם) and responded to 'the cry of the sons of Israel' (שַׁוְעָתָם); (2) God says 'I have also heard the groaning of the sons of Israel' (אֲנִי שָׁמַעְתִּי אֶת־ נַאֲקַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל), emphasizing empathy for the entire people's suffering; (3) God's entire plan to 'bring you out from under the burdens of Egypt' and 'redeem you with an outstretched arm' is motivated by compassion for the suffering people; (4) God establishes a covenant to 'take you as My people' (לְעָם), not to elevate leaders above the people. Moses and Aaron function as instruments of God's will to liberate the people, but the text's emotional and theological center is God's empathy for the oppressed masses.
